title: 雙時代之鐘

plotAndTimelineReview.chapterSpecificFinding: 1895與1945公開朗讀經核證的證言，並讓許某依法答辯；最後的彈簧阻止會抹去記憶的第二聲鐘，不再擅自改寫他人歷史。
plotAndTimelineReview.previousChapterEndingEnglish: A radar operator passing through the school offered to scoop water from the flooded workbench while they repaired the device. Despite having no connection to the mystery, he worked until dawn. By sunrise, the spring held steady. One volunteer predicted the repair would last a hundred years; Yicheng refused to make such a promise. Instead he tested the bell, documented the limits, and asked everyone to check his measurements. It was time to depart from the laboratory and return to the theatre. When Zhaoyue lifted the repaired mechanism, she knew that success would be measured not by a perfect clock, but by whether the witnesses could speak freely after it fell silent.
plotAndTimelineReview.nextChapterOpeningEnglish: Morning dew covered the theatre steps in 1895. The copper clock had stopped, but the names it guarded remained. Zhaoyue woke to find Wenbo waiting with breakfast and a letter from Yicheng. It had traveled through the final open passage during the night. The paper was creased, and the ink had spread into an enormous blue stain, yet she recognized his signature. He wrote that his father's shop was no longer threatened by bankruptcy, and that the new public archive had welcomed volunteers, including people with disabilities whose careful work was too often overlooked. Nothing in the letter suggested that the future had become perfect.

paragraphs.en: The annual gathering filled both theatres. In 1895, families brought letters and the names of relatives who had vanished. In 1945, children carried copies of those same names, protected by a new establishment devoted to public records. A former military commander sat beside a teacher and listened without demanding obedience. The idea was unfamiliar to him. He had spent his life expecting orders to move downward through ranks, yet the stories before him could not be reduced to commands. Zhaoyue took confidence from his silence. Even a person trained to command could learn to listen.
paragraphs.zh: 一年一度的聚會同時充滿兩座戲院。 1895年，家庭帶來信件與失蹤親人的名字；1945年，孩子帶來相同姓名的副本，由新成立的公共紀錄團體保護。一名退役指揮官坐在老師旁，聽著卻沒有要求服從。這對他很陌生；他一生習慣命令自上而下，如今面前的故事卻不能化成軍令。昭月從他的沉默得到信心。連習慣發號施令的人，也可能學會傾聽。

paragraphs.en: The first speaker read a biography of a messenger whom history had described only as “missing.” The account included his failures, kindness, debts, and ordinary jokes. It was not a conventional hero's portrait. Its author said that a constitution could protect rights on paper, but people still needed the courage to notice when those rights were denied. The audience listened closely. For the first time, the messenger's child heard adults discuss his father as a complicated human being rather than an imaginary figure. He wiped his eyes and held the wooden bird against his chest.
paragraphs.zh: 第一位講者朗讀一名信差的傳記。 歷史原本只寫他「失蹤」，傳記卻記下他的失敗、善意、欠債與普通笑話，不是傳統的英雄肖像。作者說，憲法可以在紙上保護權利，但人仍需要勇氣察覺權利何時受侵害。觀眾專心聽著。那名信差的孩子第一次聽大人把父親當成複雜的真人，而非幻想中的人物。他擦掉眼淚，把木鳥緊緊抱在胸前。

paragraphs.en: Xu was brought before the group to answer questions regarding his forged documents. He tried to defend his actions as necessary, then sank into a deep depression when his arguments failed. Zhaoyue did not scold him. She had no intention of offering cheap mercy, but neither would she build a new system on humiliation. The investigators presented their observations and allowed Xu to respond. He admitted that his belief in controlling history had begun as fantasy: an imaginary world where no one suffered because he had removed every cause of suffering. In practice, he had simply removed the records of those who suffered.
paragraphs.zh: 許某被帶來回答偽造文件的問題。 他先說自己的行為出於必要，辯解失敗後陷入深深沮喪。昭月沒有責罵他，也不打算輕易施予廉價的寬恕；但她不願用羞辱建立新制度。調查者提出觀察所得，讓許某回答。他承認，控制歷史的想法最初像一場幻想：他想像只要除掉苦難的原因，就不會再有人受苦。現實裡，他除掉的只是受苦者的紀錄。

paragraphs.en: A stingy businessman attended the ceremony hoping to buy exclusive rights to the archive. He offered money for the old photographs and promised to protect them from damage. Zhaoyue asked whether families would still be able to see and correct the records. He avoided the question, praising his own generosity instead. Wenbo thanked him for coming but declined the offer. They had seen what happened when one person claimed to own the evidence of many lives. Money could support conservation, but it could not replace accountability. The businessman left irritated, while several modest donors offered paper, shelves, and time without requesting control.
paragraphs.zh: 一名吝嗇商人來參加儀式，想買檔案室獨家權利。他出錢買舊照片，保證會妥善保存。昭月問，家屬是否還能看並修正紀錄？他閃躲問題，只誇自己的慷慨。文博謝謝他前來，卻婉拒了。他們已見過一人聲稱擁有眾多人生命證據的後果。金錢能支持保存，不能代替問責。商人氣沖沖離開，幾位普通捐助者反而不要求控制權，只願送紙、書架與時間。

paragraphs.en: After the reading, the commander approached the messenger's child. He admitted that he had once signed an order without examining how its language might affect the families listed beneath it. He could not reverse the past, but he offered to help locate the missing correspondence. The child looked uncertain. He was not ready to forgive a stranger simply because the man wore a serious face. Zhaoyue did not press him. Instead, she wrote down the commander's offer and gave the family a copy. An act of responsibility could begin without receiving an immediate reward, and forgiveness was not a duty that could be ordered.
paragraphs.zh: 朗讀後，退役指揮官走向信差的孩子，承認自己曾在未細看用語如何傷及名單家屬時便簽下命令。他無法倒轉過去，卻願意幫忙找失蹤信件。孩子不確定，也不願只因對方神情嚴肅就原諒。昭月沒有催促，只記下指揮官的提議，交家屬一份副本。負責任可以從沒有立即回報的行動開始，而原諒不是能被下令的義務。

paragraphs.en: The hall fell silent long enough for the youngest listeners to hear the old clock's soft ticking. Zhaoyue hoped they would remember that sound not as a threat, but as proof that they had been trusted with the truth.
paragraphs.zh: 禮堂安靜得連最小的孩子也聽見銅鐘輕輕滴答。昭月希望他們記得的不是威脅，而是自己曾被託付真相。

paragraphs.en: Yicheng gave a short explanation of the clock's mechanism so the audience could digest the concept. He intended to disable the second bell while leaving the archives intact. The decision did not mean every wound had healed. Some families remained angry; some records were permanently lost; some people could not bear to attend. Yet a quiet triumph came when the audience began reading names together without waiting for permission. Across the passage, Zhaoyue heard Wenbo's voice merge with Yicheng's. Then the repaired spring caught the second bell, and the sound that would have erased them never came.
paragraphs.zh: 以誠用簡短說明讓觀眾理解銅鐘的機制。 他打算停用第二聲鐘，卻保留檔案。這不表示所有傷口已癒合：有些家屬仍憤怒，有些紀錄永遠失去，有些人受不了而缺席。但當全場不等許可便一起朗讀姓名時，一場安靜的勝利已經發生。通道彼端，昭月聽見文博的聲音與以誠相融。接著修好的彈簧擋住第二聲鐘，那道原本會抹去眾人的聲音終究沒有響起。
